messages:
Kenji Nakamura: Dropping the latest landing page variant copy + hierarchy for the activation-focused quickstart page. Would love quick eyes on (1) above-the-fold structure, (2) what feels too “marketing-y”, (3) CTA order. Doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/quickstart-variant-outline (section “Copy v0.3”).

Alicia Perez: skimmed. overall good direction. above fold feels a little dense though.
- recommend: headline + 1 sentence subhead + 3 proof bullets + primary CTA.
- move “Benchmarks” lower; too early before we show the 3-step quickstart.
(reactions: :thumbsup: x2)

Tessa Morgan: +1 to reducing density. also the section headers are competing (same weight). If everything is H2, nothing is H2.
Suggestion:
1) Hero
2) “Get to first success in ~5 minutes” (short, numbered)
3) “Production-ready by default” (streaming, latency/cost dashboard, retries)
4) Benchmarks / perf proof
5) Troubleshooting

Kenji Nakamura: That makes sense. I was trying to lead with performance proof for retargeted folks, but yeah it’s distracting from action.
Do we want the hero to say “LLM inference” or “API” here? Trying not to sound generic.

Soojin Lee: PMM take: keep hero concrete + developer-first.
Headline option: “Ship your first Redwood inference call in minutes.”
Subhead can carry the value prop: “Low-latency, cost-aware LLM serving with hosted, dedicated, or private deploys.”
Also: careful with “X% cheaper / fastest” language unless we’re linking a specific benchmark page + date + setup.

Alicia Perez: yeah, “in minutes” is good but maybe avoid an exact number unless we can back it up. “in a few minutes” safer.
Also CTA should be code-first.
Primary CTA: “Copy curl command” or “Run quickstart” (tabs: curl / TS / Python?)
Secondary CTA: “Open Console”

Marissa Cole: For the CTA path: if we can deep link, I’d rather “Open Console checklist” vs generic console. People land there and bounce.
We can add UTM param + route to /console/onboarding? (feature-flagged, but works for most).

Ben Carter: +1 on CTA instrumentation. From ads we want the landing page to push “first request success” event. If CTA sends them to docs only, we lose them.
Could we do “Get API key” as step 1, then “Make first request” as step 2? That aligns with funnel.

Tessa Morgan: re hero wording: avoid “LLM inference platform” in headline; feels like a deck.
Maybe:
- “Make a first request. Then optimize.”
- or “From first token to production metrics.”
But keep it literal; this page is supposed to activate, not position.

Kenji Nakamura: Got it. I’ll revise to:
- Hero: “Ship your first Redwood inference call in a few minutes.”
- Subhead: “Streaming responses, latency/cost breakdowns, and reliable fallbacks—same API across hosted/dedicated/private.”
- Then quickstart steps immediately.

Soojin Lee: One more: the “Benchmarks” section copy currently says “2–3x throughput” with no context. If we keep it, add “see methodology” link + make it relative (“up to”) + specify vs baseline (e.g., naive HF serving).
Also, “enterprise-grade” phrasing—can we swap to something more dev-friendly like “SLA options + private networking when you need it”?

Alicia Perez: layout: troubleshooting should be closer to the quickstart, not at the bottom. People hit errors and scroll.
Maybe after step 3, show a collapsible “Common errors” module:
- 401 (API key)
- 429 (rate limit)
- streaming disconnect

Marissa Cole: +1 on streaming disconnect. Also permission confusion: some new users generate keys but don’t attach to project correctly. If we can mention “create key in Project Settings” w/ screenshot, fewer tickets.

Tessa Morgan: accessibility nit: if we do code tabs, ensure keyboard nav + proper aria for tablist. Also avoid light gray code on white.

Kenji Nakamura: All noted. Next pass: update hierarchy + tighten claims + pull troubleshooting up. I’ll ping when doc is updated.

Soojin Lee: cool—tag me when you update the benchmark language. I’ll also ask Ethan if we have a canonical benchmark link we can safely reference.

Kenji Nakamura: will do. Thanks all.
